Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

cooperation noun

also co-operation, cooperate, co-operate, collaborate, collaboration, work together, joint effort, partnership (working together)

classical

Cic. Phil. 2.24: societātem cum aliquō coīre (Lewis & Short)
Phaedr. 1.5.1

societās, societātis f.

noun, third declension

partnership, cooperation, joint undertaking

A union for a common purpose (Lewis & Short): to cooperate with someone is societātem coīre cum aliquō, to share a task in societāte esse. Its other common sense is society, fellowship in general (see society-people, company-firm).

Other words

  • cōnsociō, cōnsociāre, cōnsociāvī, cōnsociātum — join in, share, unite (with someone)

    verb, first conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Liv. 1.17.5: rem inter sē cōnsociant (Lewis & Short); Cic. Red. Sen. 16: cōnsilia cum aliquō cōnsociāre (Lewis & Short)

    To make something common, to go into it together: plans, power, a task.

  • cooperātiō, cooperātiōnis f. — cooperation

    noun, third declension · also used · post-classical · Quint. Decl. 16; Cassiod. (Lewis & Short)

    Rare and late, with the verb cooperārī of Christian Latin (Dominō cooperante, Vulg. Marc. 16.20); in classical prose, societās or a verb with ūnā (see together).

Examples

  • numquam est fidēlis cum potente societās

    a partnership with the powerful is never to be trustedPhaedr. 1.5.1

  • dīligentibus Deum omnia cooperantur in bonum

    for those who love God all things work together for goodVulg. Rom. 8.28 (Lewis & Short)

See also together, help, team, society, company.

SourcesLewis & Short: societas · Lewis & Short: consocio · Lewis & Short: cooperatio · Lewis & Short: cooperor

Phaedrus from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-phaedrus); the other passages as Lewis & Short quotes them.
